title: String Termination and Off-by-One Errors
platform_conditions: C99/C11 on any hosted toolchain; consequences depend on how the surrounding code consumes non-NUL-terminated buffers
security_mechanism: strncpy copies at most n bytes and pads with NUL bytes only if the source is shorter; when strlen(src) >= n it copies exactly n bytes and writes no terminator, leaving dst an unterminated char array. A later strlen/printf/strcpy on dst runs off the end into adjacent memory — both an overread (leaking whatever follows, e.g. a secret in a neighbouring buffer) and an overread-driven overflow when a copy is made from it. The same arithmetic produces off-by-one conditions: buffers sized len instead of len+1, loops that write buf[len] as the terminator into an array declared [len].

source_sink_clues.source: Strings whose length the attacker controls: usernames, paths, header values, protocol strings that reach a fixed-size copy and are later treated as C strings.
source_sink_clues.sink: strncpy into a fixed buffer followed by strlen/printf/strcpy on that buffer; any strlen on a buffer that is not provably NUL-terminated

tracking_guards: Check that the byte after a strncpy result is explicitly NUL-written (dst[sizeof(dst)-1] = '\0'), that truncation itself is detected (source length compared before copy), or that snprintf with sizeof(dst) replaces the strncpy; verify no strlen/read is applied to a buffer whose termination depends on the copy.
not_candidate_when: The buffer is explicitly terminated after every strncpy on all paths, the source is bounded by a length check that guarantees room for the terminator, or the copied region is used with explicit lengths only (never as a C string).
public_references: SEI CERT C Coding Standard: STR32-C (null-terminate byte strings), STR31-C (bounds before string ops)
